title: SSO & RBAC alignment session with Nebula Therapeutics
participants_header: Date: 2025-06-05 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62m | Recording: yes
summary: Redwood AE+SE introduced SSO/SAML/SCIM onboarding options and walked through an RBAC least-privilege proposal for Nebula's multi-tenant research org. Discussion covered audit logs retention, KMS integration options, data residency constraints for EU samples, SOC 2 evidence, and an onsite pilot for private deployment. Action items and next steps captured at the end.
topics: SSO/SAML metadata exchange and IdP mapping
SCIM provisioning cadence and group sync behavior
RBAC role model and least-privilege mapping to Nebula org structure
Audit log formats, retention, and export for SIEM
Encryption at rest KMS options (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed)
Data residency for EU projects and private deployment considerations
SOC 2/ISO artifacts and timeline for attestation
action_items: Jared Kim - Share SOC 2 Type II report and ISO27001 summary PDF by 2025-06-06
Priya Shah - Draft RBAC mapping csv (roles -> nebula groups) and post to shared drive by 2025-06-10
Samir Patel (Nebula) - Provide IdP metadata and example SCIM group names by 2025-06-09
Evan Morales - Schedule pilot runbook and propose test cases for KV cache and RBAC enforcement by 2025-06-12
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack and SOC2/ISO docs
Customer to share IdP metadata and current group naming conventions
Schedule a 2-hour technical pilot kickoff (private deployment/BYO-KMS) w/ infra team week of 2025-06-16
Agree on audit log retention policy and export format for SIEM integration
transcript:
[00:00] Jared Kim: ok everyone thanks for joining the SSO and rbac alignment session, i'm jared from Redwood, with me is priya and evan. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Lena Ortiz: doing good thanks, excited to get this moving, we've got a few constraints to throw on the table up front.
[00:14] Dr. Marco Ruiz: quick note, we need EU residency for patient-derived data, and we have strict KMS requirements for key custody.
[00:22] Priya Shah: noted. we'll outline options: hosted with customer-managed keys, and private (VPC) where keys stay in your KMS. we'll also surface tradeoffs for latency and operations.
[00:32] Samir Patel: yes, custody is a must. We can't have Redwood-managed KMS for EU datasets.
[00:37] Jared Kim: got it. on SSO, are you using SAML IdP today or OIDC?
[00:43] Hannah Lee: primary IdP is Okta, SAML 2.0, but we also have some OIDC apps. SCIM available yes.
[00:50] Evan Morales: great. the standard flow we recommend is SAML for auth + SCIM for provisioning. SCIM group sync frequency — we can do near real-time or batched; batched reduces API calls but introduces a sync lag.
[01:02] Dr. Marco Ruiz: what's the delta on permissions if group sync lags by 5-15 minutes? any risk for privilege creep?
[01:09] Priya Shah: short lag could mean a user remains in a role slightly longer, but our RBAC enforcement checks at request time against local role cache and SCIM delta events. in practice we've seen up to 30s to 2m for most customers. if you need strict immediate revocation we recommend push events from your IdP or the private deployment webhooks.
[01:27] Lena Ortiz: we will need immediate deprovisioning for contractors.
[01:31] Jared Kim: ok we'll note contractors as a high-sensitivity group and propose immediate webhook-based revocation for that group.
[01:39] Samir Patel: on RBAC model, can you show an example mapping for our org? we have teams: bench-research, clinical-ops, data-platform, external-qa.
[01:47] Priya Shah: absolutely, we usually map to three layer model: platform roles (admin, infra), team roles (team-lead, engineer), and dataset roles (read, annotate, export). for your tenants: bench-research -> annotate/read, clinical-ops -> read/export limited, external-qa -> read-only sandbox.
[02:02] Jared Kim: i'll share a csv with columns: role_id, role_name, scim_group_name, allowed_actions. that helps with least-privilege review.
[02:10] Dr. Marco Ruiz: about audit logs - format and retention. we need syslog-sent events to our SIEM and an immutable audit trail for 7 years. is that supported?
[02:19] Evan Morales: two parts: action audit and system audit. action audit logs (user actions, prompts, exports) can be exported via S3 with write-once mode and pushed to your SIEM via Kinesis or direct syslog shippers. retention for hosted account - default 90 days but we support extended retention add-on and long-term archival to your S3 with lifecycle policies. seven years is a long tail but doable via archival to your bucket with your lifecycle.
[02:39] Samir Patel: are those logs tamper-evident? we need chain-of-custody for compliance.
[02:43] Priya Shah: we use object immutability on the archival buckets and optional append-only audit ledger (hash chaining) for high assurance customers. we'll include the design doc.
[02:51] Hannah Lee: SOC2 evidence: can you give us expected artifacts and timelines?
[02:55] Jared Kim: yes we will send the SOC 2 Type II report, control matrix, and our ISO27001 scope summary. typical turnaround to get you the pack is 24-48 hours for redacted docs. for attestation, if you need your auditor access we can provide read-only views and auditor agreements.
[03:11] Dr. Marco Ruiz: we might require on-prem or air-gapped for some projects too - what's your Private deployment option?
[03:17] Evan Morales: private supports VPC-hosted control plane and on-prem packaged runtime. it can run behind your network, integrate with your KMS/HSM, and avoid cross-border data egress. latency will differ and we'll propose a pilot benchmark.
[03:29] Lena Ortiz: one more on encryption - do you support BYOK with AWS KMS and Vault HSM?
[03:35] Priya Shah: yes we support AWS KMS customer-managed keys, and bring-your-own HSM via standard PKCS#11 integrations for the private package. there are additional ops considerations we'll document.
[03:45] Samir Patel: great. can we see an example of audit log entries for a model export? specifically token-level redaction policies.
[03:50] Priya Shah: sure - audit entry includes timestamp, actor_id, action_type, resource_id, model_id, tokens_processed (redacted if PII), redaction_flags. we can redact token streams and store metadata separately.
[04:04] Dr. Marco Ruiz: how do you handle data residency when an org has mixed projects EU and US?
[04:09] Evan Morales: routing by policy. requests tied to EU project IDs route to EU region endpoints; metadata and policy can be enforced by project label. however for full isolation we recommend dedicated capacity in the region or private deployment.
[04:22] Lena Ortiz: who's the owner for entitlements in Redwood console? we want to map to our approver workflow.
[04:27] Jared Kim: the account admin role can delegate approvers. we support SAML group-to-role mapping and approval workflows via an API hook to your internal ticketing system.
[04:38] Samir Patel: on provisioning cadence, does SCIM reconcile deletes? if a user is deleted in Okta will Redwood remove all tokens and active sessions?
[04:45] Priya Shah: yes, SCIM delete triggers revocation; we also have session TTLs and can force global logout via the admin API. there's a short window if using cached tokens but we can set short TTLs for high-security groups.
[04:59] Interrupt - background noise, unclear speaker: (crosstalk)
[05:05] Hannah Lee: for auditors we also need proof of least-privilege enforcement, can Redwood generate periodic evidence of role assignments and access reviews?
[05:12] Evan Morales: we produce access reports exportable as CSV with timestamps and can schedule quarterly attestation exports. we can add reviewer sign-offs via SSO-linked approvals.
[05:23] Jared Kim: ok, let's surface the pilot scope: private deployment in EU on one node, integrate with nebula-kms, run a two-week benchmark with sample payloads, validate RBAC, SCIM provisioning and audit exports.
[05:36] Dr. Marco Ruiz: timeline? we'd like to start pilot mid-June.
[05:40] Jared Kim: target kickoff week of 2025-06-16, we'll send proposed slots.
[05:45] Samir Patel: any blockers from Redwood side for BYOK?
[05:48] Priya Shah: just an ops checklist: key wrap instructions, HSM cert exchange, and network allowlists. none are blockers but require coordination.
[05:58] Lena Ortiz: can you highlight differences vs MajorCloudAI? they suggested a single-tenant VM but we found limitations on audit exports.
[06:06] Jared Kim: difference is Redwood provides native audit export pipelines to customer buckets and an append-only ledger option; our private package includes the HSM integration patterns and full control-plane isolation. we'll include a comparison doc.
[06:18] Hannah Lee: ok i'm going to flag regulatory requirement: records retention 7 years, access logging for admin actions, and SSO SAML assertion expiry settings.
[06:27] Priya Shah: SAML assertion expiry we recommend short assertions (1-5 minutes) with refresh tokens for session continuity; we can align with your compliance policy.
[06:37] Dr. Marco Ruiz: will Redwood allow us to configure per-project encryption policies so that some projects are always encrypted with customer keys and others with Redwood-managed keys?
[06:45] Evan Morales: yes per-project KMS policy is supported in Private and Dedicated. Hosted can support via customer-owned keys for specific projects if you bucketize assets. we'll document constraints.
[06:58] Jared Kim: quick recap: we'll send SOC2 pack, RBAC csv template, pilot runbook, and schedule pilot kickoff. action owners captured.
[07:06] Lena Ortiz: thanks all, that's helpful. we'll circulate IdP metadata and confirm pilot participants.
[07:12] Meeting ends
notes: Shared artifacts: security-pack link (redwood-sec-pack.pdf), RBAC mapping template (rbac-template.csv), pilot-runbook draft (pilot-runbook.md). Customer asked for auditor access and immutable log proof. Prioritized contractor immediate deprovisioning and EU residency pilot.
